title: eCommerce Fulfillment Service Gaps in Industrial and Automotive Parts
summary: Generic eCommerce fulfillment service advice skips fitment, hazmat, and EDI. See what industrial and automotive suppliers should fix first.
body_markdown:
In this article, learn about:


-


Why advice on eCommerce fulfillment service often doesn't tell the full story


-


What fitment, hazmat, and oversized freight requirements do to an item record before an order ships


-


How adding a single online channel multiplies electronic data interchange (EDI) volume across the partners you already sell to


---


Almost every company selling an eCommerce fulfillment service is really selling warehouse space. They hold your inventory,[pick and pack](https://www.spscommerce.com/community/articles/pick-and-pack-101-methods-kpis-costs-and-tech) each order, and hand the box off to a carrier. That’s exactly what plenty of online sellers need. But industrial and automotive suppliers usually do not, because they already run warehouses and ship to distributors.


For those suppliers, the harder work starts after the box is packed. Once a new channel starts producing real orders,[electronic data interchange](https://www.spscommerce.com/community/articles/what-is-edi-electronic-data-interchange) (EDI) documents built from the item record travel back out to the distributor, retailer, or marketplace that placed it. Those records are complex for industrial and automotive parts, carrying attributes such as fitment and hazmat classification. And wrong or missing attributes result in rejected transactions, wrong-part returns, or chargebacks.


This article explains what has to be right in the item record before a new channel goes live, and what it costs when it isn’t.


**Related Reading:**ACES and PIES Explained: A Primer on Automotive Catalog Data **


## Why Does Generic Fulfillment Advice Break Down for Parts Catalogs?


Advice written for consumer goods assumes a catalog where a product has a name, a size, a color, and a price.


Parts catalogs, on the other hand, carry considerably more information:


### Fitment Data


Fitment data describes which vehicles or machines a part serves. It is usually recorded as year, make, model, and submodel, plus cross-references to the part numbers it replaces.


Fitment accuracy is often considered one of the hardest requirement in the category. A catalog of tens of thousands of parts creates far more compatibility records than a spreadsheet can hold reliably.


### Hazmat and Oversized Freight


A good share of industrial and automotive inventory ships under hazardous material rules, including:


-


Batteries


-


Aerosols


-


Solvents


-


Adhesives


-


Lubricants


All of these carry classifications that determine packaging, labeling, paperwork, and which carriers will take the shipment.


Oversized freight adds a second set of limits. Size and weight thresholds decide whether an item moves as a parcel or as freight, with the answer shifting by carrier and by destination state. Both rule sets come from the item record, so a bad classification follows every order for that part.


**Related Reading** :[Hazmat Shipping 101: Compliance Essentials for Industrial and Automotive Brands](https://www.spscommerce.com/community/articles/hazmat-shipping-101-compliance-essentials-for-industrial-and-automotive-brands) **


### Long-Tail SKUs


Parts catalogs are long-tailed by design.


A supplier may carry tens of thousands of active[stock-keeping units](https://www.spscommerce.com/community/articles/what-is-a-stock-keeping-unit-sku) (SKUs) while a few hundred drive most of the volume. The rest turn slowly and without much pattern. Stock for those slow movers often sits across several locations, contract manufacturers, and outside warehouses, so an accurate count means reconciling systems.


## How Does EDI Order Fulfillment Change When You Add a Channel?


Rather than add a fixed amount of work, a new channel multiplies documents. Weekly replenishment batches from a few distributors can become a steady stream of small orders, all of which use the same document set as a large order.


**Document**


**What it carries**


**Who sends it**


**What goes wrong**


850 Purchase Order


The order itself, line by line


Trading partner to supplier


Unrecognized part numbers reject at import


810 Invoice


Billing detail matched to the order


Supplier to trading partner


Price or quantity mismatches become deductions


856 Advance Ship Notice


Carton contents, tracking, timing


Supplier to trading partner


Late or inaccurate notices hit compliance scorecards


940 and 945 Warehouse pair


Ship instructions and shipping confirmation


Supplier and warehouse


Timing gaps leave inventory counts stale


Volume by itself is manageable, but volume increases multiply the cost of any defect already sitting in the item record, so a problem that caused one rejected transaction a week could start causing several a day.


Osborn is an industrial brush maker founded in 1887 that sells mainly through distributors such as Grainger and Fastenal.[Before it standardized EDI operations](https://www.spscommerce.com/resources/osborn/) , bad item data meant staff checked every order by hand or the company SAP system rejected it.


“Our error rates due to bad data were at 30 percent or more before SPS, today they are under 10 percent and improving rapidly,” said Josh Tobler, IT Director at Osborn.


## What Should Suppliers Check Before Turning On a New Channel?


Suppliers who launch cleanly tend to resolve four questions before the first order arrives.


1.


**Item data readiness:** whether every part number carries complete and current attributes, and which system is the authoritative source when two systems disagree.


2.


**Hazmat and oversized classification:** whether classification lives in the item record itself, and whether it is current against carrier requirements.


3.


**Trading partner mandates:** which documents each partner requires, in which version, within which window, and which of those requirements the new channel changes.


4.


**Inventory visibility:** how availability is calculated across locations, how often that number refreshes, and whether the new channel reads from the same pool the existing partners do.


## Frequently Asked Questions


### Is an eCommerce fulfillment service the same thing as a third-party logistics (3PL) provider?


Usually yes, in how the term is marketed. Most providers ranking for it offer warehousing, pick and pack, and shipping. The data connectivity that moves orders between a supplier and its trading partners is a separate capability, and suppliers often need both.


### Do we need ACES and PIES if we only sell industrial parts?


Not necessarily, since both standards are specific to the automotive aftermarket. The requirement they formalize, complete and consistent item attributes that trading partners can consume without manual correction, applies to industrial suppliers regardless of which standard names it.


### Will adding an online channel change our existing EDI setup?


It changes the volume and the mix rather than the connections themselves. More orders of smaller size move through the same document types, which raises the operational cost of any item data defect already in the catalog.

Whichever storefront a supplier picks, the connectivity behind it decides whether the new channel scales with the distributor business already in place.[SPS Fulfillment handles the EDI and item data layer](https://www.spscommerce.com/products/fulfillment/edi/) between a new channel and every trading partner it touches.


*This article is general information, not compliance guidance. Hazardous material rules are set by federal regulation and by each carrier, and they change over time. Double-check current requirements with your carriers and the right regulatory authority before you ship.*
